mali-office-du-niger-hamlets.whole: By the World Bank's own completion report, the project developed 6,209 hectares of irrigated land against a formally revised target of 6,400, including 2,700 hectares at Office du Niger, 2,200 of them at Sabalibougou and 500 at M'Bewani. It counted 247,720 direct beneficiaries against a target of 300,000, and rice yields on the large Office du Niger perimeters of 7.19 tonnes a hectare against a revised target of 6.35. The Bank disbursed US$71.72 million of a total project cost of US$88.22 million and rated the overall outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, putting the economic internal rate of return at completion at 11.7% against 34% at appraisal, and net present value at US$13.9 million against US$184.2 million; the report says the appraisal economic analysis was over-optimistic. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
mali-office-du-niger-hamlets.searched: World Bank documents API for P095091, then the 2020 Implementation Completion and Results Report on documents1.worldbank.org, read for area, beneficiaries, yields, disbursement, rating and economic return.

zambia-camdex-copper-revenue.whole: The claim collected nothing through the English courts: an academic study of sovereign debt litigation records that Camdex sued Zambia's central bank in the United Kingdom in May 1995 and obtained attachment orders on Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines revenues, that the UK orders were later dismissed, and that the second, New York case ended in an out-of-court settlement in June 1997 on terms the study does not disclose (Schumacher, Trebesch and Enderlein, ECB working paper 2135). On Zambia's side of the ledger, a policy framework paper of 10 March 1999, prepared by the Zambian authorities with IMF and World Bank staff, gives copper production of 314,000 tonnes in both 1996 and 1997, copper exports of 327,000 and 301,000 tonnes at US$1,734 and US$2,156 a tonne, real growth of 6.6% then 3.3%, and average inflation of 43.1% then 24.4%. The same paper puts debt service before rescheduling at 40.7% of exports in 1996 and 28.8% in 1997, the net present value of debt at 509.7% of exports at end-1998, and arrears to non-Paris Club bilateral creditors at about US$300 million, and says Zambia will seek relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative. That paper does not mention commercial creditors or any litigation. Its figures come from the government and the two lenders; no independent check of them was found.

penarroya-cobrac-santo-amaro-lead.whole: No figures for the smelter's lead output, revenue or taxes were found. It made lead ingots from ore mined at Boquira in the Bahian interior and operated from 1960 to 1993 (Santos and Anjos, Geologia USP Serie Cientifica, 2022; Ambiente & Sociedade, 2013), closing in December 1993 according to a 2024 research project at the Universidade da Integracao Internacional da Lusofonia Afro-Brasileira. That project also quotes a 2003 UNDP account, at second hand, that in 1974 Cobrac asked to raise its metallic lead capacity from 30,000 to 45,000 tonnes a year, and that Bahia's government refused and suggested moving the plant to the Aratu industrial centre. The same project says about 2,500 people worked there but gives no source for the figure; no workforce total appears in the peer-reviewed review of the research, where the nearest number is the 216 Cobrac workers examined in a 1983 study of lead poisoning and anaemia by Loureiro and others, a study sample rather than a headcount.
penarroya-cobrac-santo-amaro-lead.searched: Ambiente & Sociedade review of 40 years of Santo Amaro research (2013, via Redalyc), Santos and Anjos in Geologia USP Serie Cientifica (2022), and a 2024 Unilab research project; searched in Portuguese for Cobrac/Plumbum production tonnage, employment and tax figures and found none.

multan-wwtp-suraj-miani-crops.whole: The project was meant to improve living conditions for 3.6 million people in low-income communities across 21 towns. ADB approved two loans totalling US$90 million and disbursed US$49.8 million, the loans closing on 31 December 2009; 166 of 172 subprojects were completed, including 71 of 80 sewerage and wastewater subprojects, and they were finished after loan closure out of government funds. Community development and participation and incremental land development for the poor were not undertaken, and the validation report says wastewater treatment plants and landfills were still incomplete. ADB's two offices disagree on the result: the project team's completion report rated the project Successful, Relevant and highly efficient, while the Independent Evaluation Department rated it Less than Successful, less than relevant and efficient; neither account says whether the Multan plant was finished. The evaluation department also reports urban poverty in Punjab rising from 13.1% in 2005 to 16.8% in 2009, against a target of cutting the urban population in absolute poverty from 35% to 22%, diarrhoea in children under five falling from 20.3% to 14.3% between 2004 and 2010 in project towns, and a 15% fall in water- and hygiene-related patients at district hospitals in project areas between 2006 and 2009. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

shell-vila-carioca-contamination.whole: No figures for the terminal's storage capacity, the volumes it handled, its workforce or its taxes were found. Minutes of a 13 May meeting of Sao Paulo's municipal environment council for the Ipiranga district record that 'in 1940 Shell arrived in the district to store and distribute petroleum products' and that 'in 1953 they began to produce agrochemicals'; the minutes do not give the year of the meeting. A report of 6 June 2005 in Sesc Sao Paulo's magazine quotes a Shell press adviser, Luciano Frucht, saying remediation work at the fuel storage and distribution base was continuing, and records that in December 2004 the company signed an agreement with the labour prosecution service covering the health of workers and former employees; the report adds that there had still been no compensation of any kind for residents around the site. No cost was published for the remediation.
shell-vila-carioca-contamination.searched: Sao Paulo municipal environment council (CADES) minutes for the Ipiranga district, the Sesc Sao Paulo report of 6 June 2005, and searches in Portuguese for the terminal's capacity, throughput, employment and remediation cost; nothing found.

equatorial-palm-oil-jogbahn.whole: By the company's own announcements to the London market, about 7,900 hectares had been planted in Liberia since 2011, 6,470 of them at the Palm Bay estate, of which 5,156 hectares were mature enough to harvest by June 2019; 1,418 hectares were planted at Butaw, out of a concession there of 8,011 hectares. A 30 tonne-an-hour palm oil mill at Palm Bay was commissioned in September 2018, and fresh fruit bunch harvests rose from 2,000 to more than 4,000 tonnes a month over the three months to June 2019, with the oil extraction rate up from 22% to 25%. For the six months to 31 March 2019 the company reported group revenue of US$85,000 and a group loss of US$4.73 million, and revenue of US$1.16 million at its Liberian joint venture. In June 2019 it said the Butaw workforce would fall by about 155 workers, roughly 70%. These are company figures; no independent check was found.

heinda-tin-mine-myaung-pyo.whole: No production, revenue, royalty or employment figures for the mine were found. Myanmar's EITI reconciliation report for 2015-16 reports tin by state economic enterprise rather than by mine: tin and gold together under one enterprise, and tin volumes reconciled as a single line of 341 tonnes reported by companies against 323 tonnes reported by government. A 2019 Chulalongkorn University thesis puts the concession, held by Myanmar Pongpipat Co., Ltd. since 1999, at 8.23 square kilometres (2,058 acres), with an active mining zone of 1.24 square kilometres; the tonnages it gives are resource and mineable reserve estimates, not output. In a statement published in The Nation on 10 September 2017 under a mediated settlement, Myanmar Pongpipat said it had provided free water and electricity to more than 400 families near the mine, arranged a mobile medical team every month, and had raw water tested through Kasetsart University in Thailand, which it said showed the sources named in the disputed report were not contaminated; it gave no production, investment, wage or spending figures, and no independent check of these claims was found.
heinda-tin-mine-myaung-pyo.searched: Myanmar EITI reconciliation report 2015-16 (opened; tin appears only at state-enterprise level in the sections read), the 2019 Chulalongkorn University ore reserve thesis on Heinda, and the company's settlement statement in The Nation of 10 September 2017.

shell-ogbodo-isiokpo-spill.whole: No figures were found for what the Ogbodo field itself produced, or for what Shell spent on the clean-up beyond the settlement already recorded. At the level of the whole venture, Human Rights Watch reports that Shell's Nigerian joint venture produced 899,000 barrels of oil a day in 1997 from more than eighty fields, a figure taken from an environmental discussion document SPDC prepared for its own April 1998 stakeholders workshop, and that the venture accounted for more than 40% of Nigeria's total oil production, against national output averaging 2.21 million barrels a day over the first nine months of 1997 (US Energy Information Administration and Reuters, as cited by Human Rights Watch). The venture was owned 55% by the state company NNPC, 30% by Shell, 10% by Elf and 5% by Agip. Under a memorandum of understanding last negotiated in 1991, for five years and not renewed, the venture paid US$3 a barrel to the private shareholders and allowed US$2 a barrel for notional operating costs while the oil price stayed between US$12.50 and US$23 a barrel. The production figure is the company's own; no independent check of it was found.
shell-ogbodo-isiokpo-spill.searched: Human Rights Watch's 1999 Nigeria report chapter on the oil companies, which quotes SPDC's own documents and the US EIA; the chapter does not name Ogbodo or Isiokpo, and no field-level output figure for Ogbodo was found.

tayan-nuur-altain-khuder.whole: In a presentation to investors at Mines and Money Hong Kong on 25-27 March 2014, the parent company Mongolian Resources Corporation gave the mine's annual production capacity as 2.3 million tonnes, production of 2.2 million tonnes in 2013 and a target of 3.5 million tonnes for 2014, and claimed a 33% share of the Mongolian iron ore market, all as collected in SOMO's 2014 report on the global iron ore sector. SOMO, citing the Mongolian Mining Journal of March 2014, puts iron ore at about 15% of Mongolia's exports in 2013 and total iron exports at US$700 million that year. SOMO reports no revenue, tax or employment figures for the mine, and says neither Altain Khuder nor Mongolian Resources Corporation has published any annual reports or financial accounts; it cites a Moody's rating action of 8 October 2012 putting production costs for the iron ore concentrate at US$45 a tonne in 2011, which the company called outdated without giving a newer figure. The governor of Tseel soum told SOMO on 13 August 2014 that the mine was operating at 30% of capacity because of low iron ore prices. EBRD board minutes of 31 January 2012, as cited by SOMO, record a US$30 million term loan to develop the Tayan Nuur mine and US$25 million of equity in two tranches; the company's own presentation put the bank's holding at a 5% minority stake. The output figures are the company's own; no independent check was found.
tayan-nuur-altain-khuder.searched: SOMO's 2014 sector report 'Impacts of the global iron ore sector', Mongolia chapter, which collects the company's own production figures, the EBRD board minutes, the Moody's rating action and an interview with the Tseel soum governor; no company accounts were found.

bnp-rwanda-1994-arms-transfer.whole: What the money is alleged to have bought was one arms consignment. The Mail & Guardian of 15 November 1996, reporting the then unpublished third report of the UN international commission of inquiry, dated 28 October, wrote that Willem 'Ters' Ehlers admitted involvement in a June 1994 arms consignment from the Seychelles to Goma, then in Zaire on the Rwandan border: 80 tonnes of rifles, grenades and ammunition, worth well over one million rand. Ehlers said he believed the cargo was destined for the Zairean armed forces, which would not have breached the UN embargo. The report was not public at the time, and Human Rights Watch's arms project called on the UN to release it. No figure was found for what the bank earned on the transfers, and the French investigation has produced no charge or ruling.
bnp-rwanda-1994-arms-transfer.searched: Mail & Guardian report of 15 November 1996 by Stefaans Brummer on the UN commission of inquiry's third report, via the France Genocide Tutsi archive; searched for the commission's own report text and for any figure on fees the bank earned, and found neither.

yakjin-veng-sreng-2014.whole: The Phnom Penh Post reported that Yakjin's Cambodian factory employed close to 3,000 workers and that its clients included Gap and Wal-Mart. The Worker Rights Consortium describes the firm as the third largest Korean-owned factory owner in Cambodia and records the US investment firm Carlyle Group buying a majority stake in December 2013. After the strike, Yakjin sent a labour-rights consultant, Gare Smith, a lawyer and former US State Department human rights official, to Phnom Penh for about a week in mid-August; the company said his preliminary assessment indicated 'significant areas of strength as well as some areas for improvement' and that the review was still in progress, with no final report delivered at that point. No figures were found for the factory's output, exports, wages or taxes.
yakjin-veng-sreng-2014.searched: Phnom Penh Post report 'Yakjin factory under review' and the Worker Rights Consortium factory page for Yakjin Garment (last updated 2014); searched for Yakjin Cambodia output, export and wage figures and found none.

vedan-thi-vai-river.whole: Vedan's Vietnamese arm was set up on 1 August 1991 with initial investment capital of US$183 million and, by its own account in 2013, had put more than US$500 million into Vietnam and employed over 3,000 people, making monosodium glutamate, starch and modified starch, lysine, caustic soda and animal feed (Vietnam Business Forum, VCCI News). For 2024 the group reported revenue in Vietnam of US$166 million, down 4% on the year, which was 43.7% of group revenue of US$380.2 million and its largest market, and a total of 3,830 staff; the Vietnamese operation is eligible for a 15% corporate income tax rate against a normal rate of 20% (The Investor, 29 April 2025, from the group's own performance review). These are company figures; no independent check was found.
vedan-thi-vai-river.searched: VCCI News profile of Vedan Vietnam (company-supplied figures, 18 November 2013) and The Investor's report of 29 April 2025 on the group's Vietnam revenue, staff and tax rate; no output tonnage, export or tax-paid figures were found.

drc-war-economy-bank-channels.whole: The UN Panel of Experts put what this trade delivered to those running it in figures. It estimated that the Rwandan army could have made US$20 million a month simply by selling coltan, with intermediaries buying at about US$10 a kilo from small dealers against about US$200 a kilo for average-grade coltan, and that it must have made at least US$250 million over 18 months after the highest estimated costs, exporting at least 100 tonnes a month through Rwanda Metals (paragraph 130). The Panel says diamond dealers paid a 'Congo desk' 5% of the diamond value before each transaction, that a trading house with a turnover of US$4 million a month would pay US$200,000 a month, that two named dealers each provided on average US$2 million a year, and that the desk would have received about US$4 million in direct payments over two years for granting operating authorisations, citing 'very reliable sources' (paragraphs 127 and 128). Rwanda's defence spending was about 3% of GDP or 29% of its annual budget, with US$70 million allocated in the national budget, against the Panel's own estimate that transport and pay for about 25,000 Rwandan soldiers in the Congo came to US$51.6 million a year (paragraphs 110 to 113); the Panel agreed with President Kagame's description of the conflict as a self-financing war (paragraph 114). BCDI released US$1 million for SONEX as a loan in mid-1999, of which US$200,000 to US$300,000 had been reimbursed by February 2000, and the Panel reports, from sources it calls reliable, that about US$700,000 has been paid back by the RCD (paragraphs 131 and 134). Rwanda rejected the report: its government spokesman Joseph Bideri said the charges were 'without foundation' and that it 'sometimes speaks of people who do not exist, of companies which do not exist'; Uganda called the findings baseless and Burundi dismissed them as false (Mail & Guardian, 18 April 2001).

arab-bank-hamas-transfers-verdict.whole: Arab Bank was founded in Jerusalem in 1930 by Abdel Hamid Shoman and moved to Amman in 1948 when Israel was established. For 2014, the year of the verdict, it reported net profit of US$577 million, a rise of 15%, a balance sheet of US$45.6 billion and deposits of US$35 billion, up 2% on the end of 2013, with operations in 30 countries; these are the bank's own results, reported by Reuters, and no independent check of them was found. The Jordan Times, writing during the trial, said that in the Palestinian territories the bank had been the bank of choice for the international development and donor community, helping process payments for the US and European governments, the United Nations and major charities, that it maintains the Palestinian Authority account into which Israel deposits the tax and customs revenue it collects, and that it employs nearly 1,000 people across 27 branches there. The bank said it had provided routine banking services in compliance with counter-terrorism laws and had no intention of providing support to Hamas or any other known terrorist organisation.
arab-bank-hamas-transfers-verdict.searched: Reuters report of Arab Bank's 2014 results via Gulf News, and the Jordan Times profile of the bank published during the New York trial; no published figure for the 2015 settlement was found on either page, so no claim is made about it.
